audit.why: EVEN 6/10 at 51.76% over 3095 games holds — Darius owns levels 1-2 outright, Riven owns everything from 3 on.
audit.corrected: Rating kept; the early rows corrected to say so.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was Skill and Level 2 was Riven, though whys[0] says you lose any sustained fight at Level 1 and whys[1] says to stay out of his pull radius until W is up. Levels 4-5 and Level 6 were Skill though mid calls Level 6 'your clearest power spike'.
audit.why: The mirror audit has already shipped Darius / Darius / Riven / Riven / Riven / Riven / Riven on Darius's side, and my page must state the same facts from my perspective or mirror-fix overwrites it. The prose supports it: Hemorrhage plus an Apprehend pull owns levels 1-2, and Wind Slash owns 6.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3 and 4 flipped as matched full/content pairs, ratings dropped to 3/10 on the two Darius rows, and the whys rewritten so no row argues against its own side.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] says Apprehend 'roots' you, and the displacement race between Broken Wings and Apprehend was never mentioned.
audit.why: Apprehend is a pull with a slow, not a root — and it is the mirror of your own Q3 knockback: both sides carry displacement, and whoever lands it first owns the trade. Crippling Strike is also an auto-attack reset, so his burst opens on a wind-up, not on a visible cast.
audit.corrected: whys[1] restated as a pull with its real 26s rank-1 cooldown, spikes[1].text rebuilt around the displacement race, and whys[0] now names the Crippling Strike reset as the tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid states Apprehend's cooldown as '24 seconds base'.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16 — 26 seconds at rank 1. The whole gameplan is built on that window, so the number needs to be right.
audit.corrected: mid and whys[1] now carry 26 seconds at rank 1.

audit.why: The anti-heal advice is right and correctly targeted: Decimate heals him only off champions hit by the blade — the outer ring — which is exactly what the dos/don'ts already say.

edits.before: Your Q resets win level 1 if you weave autos between casts. Identify how Darius contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Hemorrhage stacks off his autos alone and you have no Ki Burst to end the trade — last-hit at range and give him nothing at Level 1.

edits.before: E shield lets you take a trade and refund his answer. Only take the trade when Darius's Apprehend is down.
edits.after: Apprehend is online: one step inside 535 units and he pulls you into five stacks. Stay out until W is up.

edits.before: Darius can stack Hemorrhage just by walking into auto range — you have no W stun yet to end trades quickly, so you lose any sustained fight at Level 1.
edits.after: Darius stacks Hemorrhage just by walking into auto range, and Crippling Strike is an auto reset — with no Ki Burst yet you lose every sustained fight at Level 1.

edits.before: Apprehend comes online and he can root you inside bleed range on command — stay out of his pull radius until your W is available.
edits.after: Apprehend comes online and pulls you into bleed range on command — 26 seconds at rank 1, so stay outside it until your W is available.

edits.before: The Apprehend cooldown is long enough to give you real trade windows; stay disciplined, engage only when it is down, and bank small HP leads.
edits.after: Apprehend's 26 seconds at rank 1 is a huge window and it is yours: commit the full chain every time he spends the pull, and bank the HP lead.

edits.before: Level 6 is the equilibrium point — your Wind Slash execute matches his Noxian Guillotine true damage, and neither side wants a straight 100-0 with both ultimates available.
edits.after: Level 6 is yours: Blade of the Exile adds range and Wind Slash executes off missing health, so Darius can no longer sit at 40% HP farming the way he did before your R existed.

edits.before: Full kit online for both of you — the lane becomes a pattern duel; your Q-W-Q-E-Q burst trades evenly with his bleed if you E out before five stacks land.
edits.after: Full kit for both and it becomes a displacement race — your Broken Wings knockback against his Apprehend pull, and whoever lands theirs first owns the whole trade.

edits.before: At Level 3 the lane flips into a pattern duel — your full Q-W-Q-E-Q rotation is online and his Apprehend has a long enough cooldown (24 seconds base) to give you clean windows. The rule is simple: when Apprehend is down, you commit fully — Q in, W-stun, complete the chain, and E out before bleed hits five stacks. When Apprehend is up, give nothing and last-hit at Q range. Level 6 is your clearest power spike: Wind Slash turns every fight where he is even slightly low into an execute, and Darius cannot just stand in the lane at 40% HP the way he could before you had your R.
edits.after: At Level 3 the lane flips into a pattern duel — your full Q-W-Q-E-Q rotation is online and Apprehend is 26 seconds at rank 1, which is a very long window to work in. The rule is simple: when Apprehend is down, commit fully — Q in, W-stun, complete the chain, and E out before bleed hits five stacks. When it is up, give nothing and last-hit at Q range. Level 6 is your clearest power spike: Wind Slash turns every fight where he is even slightly low into an execute, and Darius cannot stand in lane at 40% HP the way he could before you had your R.
